paper.title: An Efficient Algorithm for Cooperative Semi-Bandits

unmapped: Network of N agents on an undirected communication graph with independence number alpha_1; each agent v is activated independently each round with probability q(v); network regret sums losses of active agents
Neighbors of active agents receive their semi-bandit feedback (one-hop sharing) and exchange local information
Each agent knows its own activation probability q(v); tuning uses the total mass Q and the independence number alpha_1 (learner knows Q and alpha_1)
settings.definition_quote: At each time step t, some agents v belonging to a communication network G are asked to make a prediction x_t(v) belonging to a subset A of {0,1}^k and pay a (linear) loss <x_t(v), l_t> where l_t in [0,1]^k is chosen adversarially by an oblivious environment. ... The decision set is a subset A of {a in {0,1}^k : sum_i a_i <= m}

unmapped: Network of N agents on an undirected communication graph with independence number alpha_1; each agent v is activated independently each round with probability q(v); network regret sums losses of active agents

settings.definition_quote: For each communication network G with independence number alpha_1 there exist cooperative semi-bandit instances for which the regret of any learning algorithm satisfies R_T = Omega(Q sqrt(mkT alpha_1/Q)).

bound.expression_latex: \frac{3 Q m \log k }{\eta} + 3 Q \eta kT\left(\frac{k}{Q}\alpha_1+m\right) +\frac{\alpha_1 \, k \, T}{\beta}

symbols.Q: total activation probability mass sum_v q(v)
symbols.alpha_1: independence number of the communication network
symbols.beta_tr: truncation parameter beta of the geometric resampling
symbols.d: paper's k: dimension of binary decision vectors (number of base arms)

tuning: zeta is the Laplace density 2^{-k} exp(-||z||_1)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If $\zeta$ is the Laplace density $z\mapsto\zeta(z)=2^{-k}\exp\brb{-\lno{z}_1 }$, $\eta >0$, and $0 < \beta \le 1/ (\eta k)$, then then the regret of our \coopftpl{} algorithm (Algorithm~\ref{FTPL}) satisfies \[ R_T \leq \frac{3 Q m \log k }{\eta} + 3 Q \eta kT\left(\frac{k}{Q}\alpha_1+m\right) +\frac{\alpha_1 \, k \, T}{\beta} \;. \]

results.notes: Network regret max_a E[...] against oblivious losses, recorded as pseudo-regret. Polynomial compute given an efficient linear optimization oracle over A (Proposition 1: per-agent complexity O(T^{3/2} c sqrt((alpha_1/Q+1)/m))).

symbols.Q: total activation probability mass sum_v q(v)
symbols.alpha_1: independence number of the communication network
symbols.d: paper's k: dimension of binary decision vectors (number of base arms)

tuning: eta = sqrt(3 m log(k) / (5 k T (k alpha_1/Q + m)))

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In particular, tuning the parameters $\eta,\beta$ as follows \beta = \left\lfloor \frac{1}{k \eta}\right\rfloor and \eta = \sqrt{\frac{3m\log(k)}{5kT\left(\frac{k}{Q}\alpha_1+m\right)}} ... yields \[ R_T \le 2Q\sqrt{ 15 mkT\log(k)\left(\frac{k}{Q}\alpha_1+m\right)} \;. \]

results.notes: Tuning requires knowledge of T, k, m, Q and alpha_1.

symbols.Q: total activation probability mass sum_v q(v)
symbols.alpha_1: independence number of the communication network
symbols.d: paper's k: dimension of binary decision vectors

conditions: holds for every communication network with independence number alpha_1
hard instances activate only agents of a maximum independent set, each with the same probability q, so Q = alpha_1 q

source.label: t:lower-bound
source.quote: For each communication network $\cG$ with independence number $\alpha_1$ there exist cooperative semi-bandit instances for which the regret of any learning algorithm satisfies \[ R_T = \Omega \brb{Q \sqrt{mkT \alpha_1/Q}}\;. \]

results.notes: Proof reduces to alpha_1 independent single-agent semi-bandit problems using the known Omega(sqrt(mkT)) lower bound.
